scenario: Chinese optical transceivers and data center equipment
caveat: Demo scenario. Signals are sourced; the transceiver ban is reported, not published. Parts marked with placeholders use demo values to be replaced with student research (Sayari and real part numbers). Nothing here is a legal or compliance finding.

signals.title: FCC component rule (FCC 26-50)
signals.summary: The FCC can deny new equipment authorization to a device containing a logic-bearing hardware component from a Covered List producer, including Western-branded switches and servers.
signals.confidence: Final rule. Applies to new authorizations only. Does not cover software or firmware. Production-location entries (such as foreign-made routers) do not trigger it unless the producer is listed.

signals.title: Reported FCC ban on new Chinese transceiver models
signals.summary: The FCC is reported to be drafting a ban on new models of Chinese optical transceivers, possibly starting with the 3.2T generation, with a possible exemption for modules whose bill-of-materials value is at least 65% U.S.-sourced.
signals.confidence: No public FCC text. Start generation, timing, and the 65% threshold come from Reuters and analyst reports and are treated as assumptions. InnoLight, Eoptolink, Dongshan Precision, and TFC are not on the Covered List.

signals.title: S. 5548, Securing National Security Systems from Chinese Optical Transceivers Act
signals.summary: Would bar federal procurement of transceivers from InnoLight, Eoptolink, and designated adversary-linked makers, and of products with their firmware, software, or component parts, for national security systems.
signals.confidence: Introduced and referred to committee. Takes effect five years after enactment. Agencies may still buy for systems that are not critical.

signals.title: Zhongji Innolight added to the 1260H list
signals.summary: The Department of War added Zhongji Innolight to its list of Chinese military companies.
signals.confidence: The listing limits direct Department of War contracts with listed companies. It does not ban products government-wide.

signals.title: Foreign-made consumer routers on the Covered List
signals.summary: New models of foreign-produced consumer-grade routers cannot be authorized unless the Department of War or Homeland Security grants a conditional approval.
signals.confidence: In force. Several approvals end between October 2027 and February 2028.

signals.title: Foreign-made power inverters on the Covered List
signals.summary: New models of foreign-produced power inverters cannot be authorized unless the Department of War or Homeland Security grants a conditional approval.
signals.confidence: In force. Definitions were narrowed on August 20, 2026. Whether data center UPS equipment is in scope should be checked against the definition.
